question: What is the main goal of the Safe Motherhood Initiative?

options.B: To increase the national birth rate
options.C: To reduce maternal mortality and morbidity
options.D: To eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants

explanation: You've got this! The Safe Motherhood framework was set up specifically to lower the rates of death and severe illness linked to pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h1)

question: Why do we view the parts of safe motherhood as a continuous safety net?

options.A: Because every woman must pay a single flat fee for all services
options.B: Because skipping one phase increases the risk of poor outcomes
options.C: Because antenatal care replaces the need for postnatal visits
options.D: Because all pregnant women require emergency surgery

explanation: Think of it like a chain: each stage of safe motherhood builds on the last to keep both mother and baby protected every step of the way! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h1)

question: Which supplement is most important to give before pregnancy to help prevent birth defects?
explanation: Folic acid is a superstar vitamin! Taking it before and during early pregnancy greatly lowers the risk of neural tube defects like spina bifida. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: How does proper birth spacing protect a mother's health?

options.A: It gives the mother's body time to recover nutrients and strength
options.B: It eliminates the need for any antenatal checkups
options.C: It completely prevents the onset of gestational diabetes
options.D: It guarantees that the next baby will be born full-term

explanation: Giving the body a break between pregnancies allows nutrient stores to refill, making future pregnancies much safer for mum. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: What is a standard check done during a routine antenatal clinic (ANC) visit?

options.A: Screening for lifelong hereditary blood disorders
options.B: Performing routine pelvic ultrasounds every week
options.C: Checking maternal blood pressure and urine protein
options.D: Measuring daily caloric intake and physical activity

explanation: Spotting changes in blood pressure and checking urine for protein helps us catch early signs of pre-eclampsia. Great nursing practice! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 20 weeks ANC gets mosquito nets and iron supplements. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To determine the exact genetic sex of the baby
options.B: To induce early labor in high-risk situations
options.C: To prevent malaria and treat or prevent anemia
options.D: To stop morning sickness during the first trimester

explanation: Malaria and low blood (anemia) are major risks in pregnancy, so nets and iron are standard lifesavers in our clinics. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: What is the main use of a partograph during labor?

options.A: To monitor labor progress and detect prolonged labor early
options.B: To measure the mother's daily nutritional intake
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: To record the baby's immunization schedule after birth

explanation: The partograph is a midwife's best friend! It gives a clear picture of how labor is going so you can spot trouble early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: Why is putting traditional substances like saliva or dung on a newborn's umbilical cord dangerous?

options.A: It permanently stains the baby's skin around the abdomen
options.B: It prevents the infant from absorbing breast milk
options.C: It causes the umbilical cord to fall off too quickly
options.D: It introduces harmful bacteria that can cause severe infections like tetanus

explanation: The cord stump is a direct highway to the baby's bloodstream. Unclean substances easily bring in fatal germs like tetanus or sepsis. Keep it clean and dry! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal death worldwide?
explanation: Heavy bleeding after delivery (postpartum hemorrhage) is one of the top dangers new mothers face globally. Knowing how to manage it is key for every nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: What makes a comprehensive emergency obstetric care (EmONC) center different from a basic one?

options.A: The ability to perform blood transfusions and Caesarean sections
options.B: The presence of pediatricians in the delivery room at all times
options.C: The requirement that mothers stay in the hospital for a full month
options.D: The exclusive use of traditional herbal remedies for pain

explanation: When things get tough, a comprehensive center can handle surgeries like C-sections and give blood transfusions—things basic clinics can't do. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: When does the postnatal period officially start?

options.A: Two weeks after the infant is discharged home
options.B: Immediately after the delivery of the placenta
options.C: When the mother first notices breast milk coming in
options.D: At the start of the third trimester of pregnancy

explanation: The postnatal phase kicks off right after the placenta is delivered and runs through the first six weeks of motherhood. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: Why do new mothers need close nursing watch right after delivery?

options.A: Because the mother is at high risk for hemorrhage and infection
options.B: Because the newborn baby requires constant intravenous fluids
options.C: Because mothers cannot produce milk during the first week
options.D: Because routine vital signs are no longer necessary after birth

explanation: The body goes through massive changes right after birth, making those early hours prime time for bleeding and infections. Vigilance saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: What is the main focus of post-abortion care (PAC) services?

options.A: Preventing the client from ever becoming pregnant again
options.B: Filing legal reports against the client in every single case
options.C: Requiring mandatory psychiatric admission for all patients
options.D: Treating incomplete abortion and managing life-threatening complications

explanation: PAC is all about emergency medical care: stopping bleeding, clearing the womb safely, and treating dangerous infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: Why is family planning counseling a key part of post-abortion care?

options.A: To ensure the client conceives again within the next month
options.B: To fulfill a hospital administrative requirement unrelated to health
options.C: To help the client prevent future unintended pregnancies and repeat procedures
options.D: To punish the client for experiencing a pregnancy loss

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps clients protect their health and avoid another unplanned pregnancy down the line. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: How do nurse-led community outreach programs help improve maternal health in rural Nigeria?

options.A: By educating families and encouraging them to seek care at health facilities
options.B: By providing free vehicles to every pregnant woman in the village
options.C: By replacing the need for doctors and hospitals in all situations
options.D: By banning traditional birth attendants from practicing entirely

explanation: Outreach bridges the gap! By teaching families to spot danger signs, we help them get to the clinic early when help is most effective. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)

question: A rural clinic nurse finds that many women prefer giving birth at home. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Engage community leaders and educate women on the safety of facility delivery
options.B: Report all pregnant women who plan home births to the local police
options.C: Close the clinic until the women agree to come in voluntarily
options.D: Ignore the practice since home delivery has no real risks

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with village leaders builds trust and helps women see the safety and benefits of delivering at a health facility. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)
